question: What fish and freshwater-site evidence do two molecular Anguilla studies report for Cagayan Valley and the adjoining Cordillera, and can their records be represented as app occurrences?

studyReviews.citation: Jamandre, B. W. D., Shen, K. N., Yambot, A. V., & Tzeng, W. N. (2007). Molecular phylogeny of Philippine freshwater eels Anguilla spp. (Actinopterygii: Anguilliformes: Anguillidae) inferred from mitochondrial DNA. Raffles Bulletin of Zoology, Supplement 14, 51–59.

qualityNotes: The abstract says DNA was extracted from nine eels, while the methods say 24 freshwater eels were collected and the sampling table groups specimen numbers across the sites. The source does not clearly reconcile the total collection with the molecularly analysed subset; do not treat every table assignment as independently DNA-validated.

The figure is a locator map without station coordinates. Field collection dates, named reaches, voucher accession identifiers, and a specimen-to-sequence accession crosswalk were not established in the reviewed article.
The source calls Buguey, Casili and Abulug part of the Cagayan River system. The Abulug name is not independently crosswalked to the Apayao-Abulug basin reach or its geometry.
Preserve the source's subspecies labels verbatim pending a current specialist taxonomic crosswalk; the article is a historical molecular phylogeny, not a current distribution survey.
studyReviews.rights: The PDF states copyright by Academia Sinica and the National University of Singapore. No item-specific open license or reuse permission was identified in the reviewed PDF. No table, map, sequence or numeric result is reproduced here.

Identification of Tropical Freshwater Eels, Anguilla spp., in Cagayan River, Philippines. The Philippine Agricultural Scientist, 105(3), 226–235. https://doi.org/10.62550/abc001021
qualityNotes: The official article landing page reports Cagayan River and molecular identifications across glass-eel, elver and yellow-eel stages, but gives no station, named reach, coordinates, or field sampling dates in the abstract.
Only the publisher/UPLB article record and its abstract were reviewed; the linked PDF could not be retrieved by the research reader. No full-text table or supplementary sample data were checked.
Publication and received/revised dates are not field dates. Do not date the Cagayan River records to the article year.
studyReviews.rights: The official landing page reviewed here did not establish an item-specific reuse license. No full-text or reuse permission is inferred.

crossSourceAssessment.interpretation: Taxon-label overlap between two papers is a useful follow-up lead, not an independent abundance trend or continuous river distribution. The study designs, sampling dates, exact localities, taxonomic conventions and molecular sample subsets have not been reconciled.
crossSourceAssessment.regionalWaterScope: The 2007 paper provides leads for the Chico River in Kalinga (CAR) and three source-named waterbodies in Cagayan (Region II). The 2022 abstract adds only a broad Cagayan River lead. The Cagayan River system crosses regional boundaries; no reach geometry or basin-wide coverage is implied.

disposition.reason: The sources are useful historical freshwater research leads, but the 2007 molecular sample denominator is unresolved, neither study supplies enough verified reach/date/voucher crosswalks for a current occurrence assertion, the 2022 full text was not reviewed, and reuse rights were not established.

nextAction: Continue the Region II waterbody/source sweep with other independently accessible Cagayan Valley river, lake, reservoir, and wetland studies. Keep the eel records in research review until sample-level locality, collection dates, voucher or sequence identifiers, current taxonomic status, and suitable reuse terms are confirmed.

sources.supports: Full nine-page primary article; citation, methods, source-named sites, sample denominator inconsistency, and reported eel labels.
Official UPLB/PAS article record and abstract, publication metadata, broad Cagayan River scope, and author-reported molecular taxa.
